newsitem.title: FRANCE: TPS surpassing subscriber goal, chairman says.
newsitem.headline: TPS surpassing subscriber goal, chairman says.

text.p: Television par Satellite (TPS) has already signed up 105,000 subscribers and should have 300,000 by the end of the year, 50,000 more than its initial goal, president Patrick Le Lay said on Wednesday.

In an interview on French television LCI, he said the 2.5 billion francs earmarked for the new digital satellite television system by its founders should enable it to reach a million subscribers in four years.

Asked if TPS would meet its goal of 250,000 subscribers by the end of the year, he responded, "More than that. We should be at around 300,000. I think we should reach the goal we set for the end of the year by the end of June".
Once the system reached a million subscribers, "this would be a business worth between six and 10 billion francs," Le Lay said.
TPS, one of two French digital satellite television offerings, was launched late last year. The other, CanalSatellite, was launched by Canal Plus earlier in 1996.
It is controlled by terrestrial TV channel M6-Metropole TV and its parents, Lyonnaise des Eaux and Luxembourg's CLT, itself a part of Audiofina.
Terrestrial channel TF1 also has a 25 percent stake in TPS, and public channels France 2 and France 3 together with France Telecom hold the remaining 25 percent.
